name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Iran's IRGC says two supertankers were disabled by mines in Hormuz on 11 Nov; traffic remains heavily restricted
state: Reuters reported that two supertankers were disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz on the night of 11 Nov; Iran's IRGC said they hit mines after using a route it calls unauthorised, which is not independently verified (MarineLink, 12 Nov). Iran's army said another tanker struck a mine and caught fire on 11 Nov, and Tehran continues to restrict transits to routes it authorises (Euronews, 11 Nov). G7 foreign ministers on 11 Nov demanded Iran halt attacks on shipping.
for_you: Seafarers and shipowners using the Gulf face direct risk; UK-linked vessels should follow UKMTO guidance. Importers of Gulf oil, gas and goods are exposed to delays and higher costs.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded by Iranian restrictions and repeated attacks on ships, 10–11 Nov

sources.title: MarineLink (Reuters) — Two oil supertankers explode in Strait of Hormuz, IRGC says
Euronews — Oil prices rise as investors monitor shipping disruption in the Strait of Hormuz
The Media Line — G7 demands end to Iranian shipping attacks

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
